title: DamSustain: A Flexible Framework for Large‐Scale Vector‐Based Modeling and Direct Reservoir Optimization
content:
Abstract

Reservoirs affect the global water cycle, yet their optimization is hindered by simplified modeling frameworks. Earlier methods typically optimize parameters outside a river model by treating dams as isolated spatial nodes. In these setups, reservoir inflows are calculated by adding time-lagged outflows from upstream to static local contributions extracted from pre-simulated flows. While efficient for reservoir-level objectives like hydropower, this node-to-node approach ignores physical routing within river reaches, missing the reach-scale variables that determine downstream flow patterns. Here, we present DamSustain, a framework integrating satellite-informed reservoir models and an optimization module directly into the mizuRoute river model. By resolving river dynamics throughout the optimization phase, DamSustain allows reach-based objectives, such as maintaining natural flow variability, to directly guide reservoir management. We evaluated this framework in the Yangtze River basin by optimizing 19 large hydropower dams against a benchmark node-based setup. Results show that DamSustain increases total hydropower generation by 4.3% while simultaneously reducing downstream flow alteration by 2.7% relative to a no-optimization baseline. In contrast, policies derived from the node-based approach achieve a smaller hydropower gain of 2.3% but inadvertently degrade the downstream flow regime. This divergence occurs because the simplified setup omits channel attenuation and dynamic lateral inflows, generating policies that become hydrologically inconsistent when transferred to the physically routed river. These findings show that explicitly incorporating routing dynamics during policy search substantially reduces this structural mismatch, enabling more physically consistent trade-offs between energy and environmental benefits.
